mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) above 6% triggers a recessionary demand shock that depresses corporate earnings and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered recession episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% over two months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1,000,000 units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing market downturn that reduces household wealth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% combined with a concurrent decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 signals a rapid labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer demand and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS falls by >100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters indicates a broad-based demand slump, which compresses earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 1% annualized for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
